document: NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Acute Radiation Syndromes Due to Solar Particle Events
section: Section 3.2: Prodromal Radiation Sickness & Clinical Latency
summary: Clinical protocol for managing acute radiation exposure and Acute Radiation Syndrome (ARS) during high-energy solar storms.
protocol_steps: Immediate Action: Terminate all Extravehicular Activity (EVA) immediately and retreat to spacecraft storm shelter (SPE storm haven / water-walled module).
Shielding Optimization: Position water storage containers and polyethylene bricks around crew resting berths to maximize hydrogenous shielding mass.

Prodromal Symptom Monitoring: Initiate vital sign logging every 15 minutes. Prodromal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, fatigue) typically manifest 1 to 4 hours post-exposure for doses > 500 mGy and up to 48 hours for doses 250-500 mSv.
Medical Countermeasures: Administer Ondansetron (4mg to 8mg PO) for nausea prophylaxis if crew member reports emetic discomfort.
Hydration Protocol: Maintain oral electrolyte hydration at 150-200 mL/hour to counter fluid shifts and hypovolemia.
Ground Telemetry Sync: Package blood dosimeter readings and chronological symptom logs for high-priority burst transmission to Earth upon comms re-acquisition.
citations: JSC-CN-35747 (2016), NASA Human Research Program Space Radiation Element.

document: NASA Technical Brief: Spacecraft Internal Atmospheric Quality and Carbon Dioxide Management
section: Section 4.1: Acute Hypercapnia Protocol and ECLSS Scrubber Failure
summary: Emergency management procedures for elevated spacecraft cabin PCO2 resulting from regenerative scrubber degradation.
protocol_steps: Metabolic Load Reduction: Command all crew members to halt physical exercise and vigorous manual operations immediately to reduce internal CO2 production by 60%.

Environmental Triage: Confirm oxygen partial pressure (PO2) and SpO2. If SpO2 is nominal (>95%) while ambient PCO2 is >7.5 mmHg, rule out primary respiratory/hypoxic distress and diagnose pure environmental hypercapnia.
ECLSS Reconfiguration: Transition primary Solid Amine Vacuum Desorption (SAVD) or Carbon Dioxide Removal Assembly (CDRA) from primary bed to secondary redundant bed.
Lithium Hydroxide (LiOH) Canister Deployment: If automated CDRA fails to arrest CO2 climb within 15 minutes, unbox and manually install auxiliary non-regenerative LiOH emergency absorption canisters.
Emergency Respiratory Protection: If ambient PCO2 exceeds 12.0 mmHg (1.6%), order crew to don Portable Breathing Apparatus (PBA) or Quick-Don masks supplying 100% O2 to prevent hypercapnic narcosis.
Ventilation Scrub: Inspect inter-module air diffusers and ventilation fans to prevent localized 'CO2 pocketing' around crew heads during microgravity rest.
citations: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 Rev C; NASA JSC Space Medicine Clinical Guidance 2023.

document: NASA Crew Health Care System (CHeCS): Cardiovascular Emergencies & Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS)
section: Section 3.1: In-Flight Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS), Myocardial Infarction & Cardiac Arrest
summary: Immediate resuscitation and pharmacologic stabilization protocol for acute chest pain, suspected myocardial infarction (heart attack), and cardiac arrest in microgravity.
protocol_steps: Immediate Patient Rest & High-Flow Oxygen: Command patient to cease all physical movement immediately. Position in semi-reclined resting posture and apply 100% oxygen via Non-Rebreather mask or PBA at 10-15 L/min.

Defibrillator Deployment & Rhythm Analysis: Retrieve Crew Medical Kit Defibrillator (Tempus Pro / AED). Attach multifunction defibrillator pads (right anterior infraclavicular and left mid-axillary line) to assess for shockable arrhythmias (VF / Pulseless VT).

Pharmacological Countermeasures (Acute Chest Pain): If systolic BP > 100 mmHg, administer chewable Aspirin 324 mg (four 81 mg tablets) and Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingually every 5 minutes (max 3 doses). Hold Nitroglycerin if SBP < 90 mmHg or heart rate < 50 bpm.

Microgravity CPR Restraint System (CMRS): In event of pulseless arrest, rapidly strap patient to Crew Medical Restraint System (CMRS); operator must anchor feet in restraint loops to deliver 100-120 compressions/min (5-6 cm depth) against zero-g recoil.
Advanced Resuscitation Protocol: Prepare Epinephrine 1 mg (1:10,000 IV/IO) every 3-5 minutes if cardiac arrest persists. Establish peripheral IV or sternal intraosseous (IO) access via Fast1 kit.
citations: NASA JSC Space Medicine Operations Clinical Practice Guidelines; ISS CHeCS Medical Checklist Rev E.

document: NASA Human Research Program: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
section: Section 2.4: Intracranial Pressure Shifts and Visual Acuity Management
summary: Clinical protocol for assessing and managing cephalad fluid shifts, optic nerve sheath swelling, and progressive hyperopic refractive shifts in microgravity.
protocol_steps: Diagnostic Assessment: Perform optical coherence tomography (OCT) or fundoscopy to quantify papilledema and optic disc swelling. Record visual acuity changes using Snellen chart.
Countermeasure - Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP): Apply 20 to 30 mmHg LBNP for 2 hours daily during rest cycles to draw fluid footward and re-establish terrestrial venous pressure gradients.

Resistive Exercise Compliance: Verify crew adherence to Advanced Resistive Exercise Device (ARED) protocol; limit high-intensity Valsalva maneuvers during deadlifts that spike transient central venous pressure.
Fluid Distribution Management: Adjust dietary sodium intake to < 2,300 mg/day to reduce total extracellular fluid volume expansion.
Refractive Correction: Issue temporary adjustable spaceflight corrective lenses to compensate for progressive hyperopic visual shifts.
citations: NASA HRP SANS Evidence Book (2022); NASA Johnson Space Center Clinical Practice Guidelines.

document: NASA Generic Flight Rules: EVA Crew Health and In-Suit Decompression Procedures
section: Flight Rule B13-104: Real-time In-Suit Physiological Anomaly Criteria
summary: Threshold criteria mandating immediate EVA termination and treatment for suspected in-suit decompression sickness (DCS).
protocol_steps: Mandatory In-Suit Termination Triggers: Sustained heart rate > 85% HR_max for > 5 minutes, sustained SpO2 < 90% for > 60 seconds, or dosimeter accumulation rate > 5.0 mSv/hr.
Crew Recall Procedure: Lead spacewalker instructs secondary crew member to begin umbilical wrap and tool stowage; return to airlock under Buddy-Check protocol within 12 minutes.

Pre-Breathe & Hyperbaric Treatment: If joint pain or bends symptoms manifest post-ingress, repressurize suit to maximum operating pressure (8.3 psid) on 100% O2 to establish in-suit hyperbaric bubble resorption.
citations: NASA Flight Operations Directorate (FOD) Flight Rule Book Vol B.

document: NASA Human Research Program: Behavioral Health and Performance in Long-Duration Exploration Missions
section: Section 5.1: Sleep Loss, Circadian Disruption, and Acute Cognitive Fatigue
summary: Protocol for counteracting circadian phase desynchrony, chronic sleep debt, and cognitive performance degradation during confined deep-space flight.
protocol_steps: Objective Fatigue Audit: Review PVT (Psychomotor Vigilance Task) scores; if reaction time lapses exceed 3 standard deviations above baseline, restrict crew member from safety-critical manual flight operations.

Dynamic Lighting Adjustment: Shift habitat Solid State Lighting Modules (SSLM) to blue-enriched white light (460 nm peak) during mission wake phase, and dim to red-shifted low-lux mode 2 hours prior to sleep cycle.

Pharmacological Countermeasures: Administer low-dose Melatonin (0.3mg to 0.5mg PO) 30 minutes before sleep period if phase advance is required; avoid long-acting hypnotics (Zolpidem) unless approved by CMO.
Sleep Environment Hygiene: Verify crew sleeping berth sound dampening meets NC-40 acoustic criteria and carbon dioxide ventilation ducting maintains > 15 CFM airflow to prevent local CO2 pooling.
citations: NASA HRP Behavioral Health & Performance Evidence Report (2021).
